name: DDRK SABER2 fuse and perceptual sharpen
plain: Two latent filters that run inside the sampler. SABER on images blurs flat areas of the latent with a 3×3 average, keeping edges. On video, it pulls unstable pixels toward a running average of past steps, not past frames. The sharpen adds fine and coarse detail back, weighted away from flat areas.
math:
z(t)=(t−mean)/std per batch item; gate g(t)=sigmoid(2z).
Image: w=f(1−g((|Lap₃x|+|x−blur₅x|)/2)); x←x(1−w)+blur₃(x)·w. f=fusion 0.35.
Video: chaos=g(var over last 3 step latents); e=.7e+.3x; x←x(1−chaos·f)+e·chaos·f.
Sharpen: x+=s(.6 clamp(d₃)+.4 clamp(d₅)), d_k=(x−blur_k)·(1−flatness), clamp ±.6, flatness weight off on the final step.
Dynamic threshold used elsewhere: only under σ≤ratio·σ_max; pixels above the 99.5th percentile of |x̂₀| are pulled to that value, a per-pixel cap with no division by s.
